test_intent: Verify that CallbackQueryHandler.CanHandle returns false when the update has an explicitly null CallbackQuery field.
reason: Duplicate of CanHandle_WithoutCallbackQuery_ReturnsFalse. An update with CallbackQuery=null and an update with a Message set both exercise the same code path: no callback query present, return false. The explicit null variant adds no distinct coverage. No replacement needed; the existing non-callback-query test covers this behavior.

test_intent: Verify that HandleUserMessageAsync does not crash when the message has no From user (system message).
reason: Current test uses Assert.Pass which provides no behavioral verification -- it only confirms the method returned without throwing. The named behavior (graceful handling of system messages with null From) is a real bot contract: the handler must not crash on system messages. Rewrite to assert that moderation was NOT invoked (e.g., ModerationServiceMock.Verify(CheckMessageAsync, Times.Never)) or that the method returned early without side effects.

test_intent: Verify that HandleUserMessageAsync skips processing when the message sender is a bot.
reason: Current test uses Assert.Pass which provides no behavioral verification. The named behavior (ignoring bot messages) is a real bot contract: the handler should not process messages from bots. Rewrite to assert that moderation was NOT invoked (e.g., ModerationServiceMock.Verify(CheckMessageAsync, Times.Never)) to confirm the message was actually skipped rather than silently processed.

test_intent: Verify that when a user has an active captcha, their message is deleted via the Telegram API and processing stops.
reason: Strong test with meaningful assertion using MessageEnvelope and FakeTelegramClient.WasMessageDeleted to verify actual Telegram API side effects. Tests a real and important bot contract: messages from users pending captcha are deleted. Uses proper envelope tracking pattern. Moderate maintenance risk due to mock setup complexity, but the assertion quality justifies keeping it.

test_intent: Verify that when a user is in the banlist, HandleUserMessageAsync delegates to UserBanService.HandleBlacklistBanAsync.
reason: Clean test with meaningful mock verify assertion. Tests a critical bot contract: blacklisted users are routed to the ban service. The assertion verifies the correct delegation call with the right parameters. Moderate maintenance risk from factory setup, but the behavior is high-value and well-tested.

test_intent: Verify that club members skip moderation entirely -- CheckMessageAsync is never called for users with a registered club username.
reason: Clean test with meaningful negative mock verify (Times.Never). Tests a real bot contract: club members bypass moderation. The assertion correctly verifies that moderation was not invoked, which is the defining behavior of the club user path. Moderate maintenance risk from factory setup, but the behavior is meaningful and well-tested.
